name: Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit CSV
notes: Integrated as a live reference catalog from the public CSV release assets. It improves source discovery and coverage mapping, but CyberDecisionEngine does not execute listed third-party tools automatically.

name: OSINT Framework
notes: Integrated as a curated local reference catalog from arf.json. CyberDecisionEngine does not run its worker, deploy its web UI, or execute listed third-party tools automatically.

name: Social Media OSINT Tools Collection
notes: Curated list only; no executable code or third-party visual interface is run by CyberDecisionEngine.

name: Social Analyzer
notes: Powerful but heavy WebDriver/AGPL runtime. Keep disabled unless the deployment explicitly accepts the license and resource profile. No third-party visual interface is exposed.

name: User Scanner
notes: Executed by command inside the isolated OSINT sidecar with no proxy rotation, no loud modules, no NSFW modules, no external visual interface and bounded timeouts.

name: socid_extractor
notes: Approved profile enrichment tool. It runs by command inside the OSINT sidecar, enriches already discovered public profile URLs, uses no browser, no API keys, no cookies and bounded timeouts.

name: Github Dorks
notes: Approved as dork template reference. Runtime GitHub API execution remains separate and must use official tokens/rate limits.

name: GitHound
notes: Candidate for a future dedicated GitHub exposure sidecar. Requires GitHub token and strict rate limits. Dashboard/cloud features must stay disabled.

name: Instaloader
notes: Candidate only for public Instagram profile metadata with no login, no browser cookies, no stories, no private profiles and low request volume.

name: CrossLinked
notes: Useful concept for public employee-name discovery, but not bundled by default due GPL license and search-engine scraping behavior.

name: Alfred/Tookie OSINT
notes: Not integrated because it overlaps with Sherlock/user-scanner and includes Selenium/webscraper paths that add weight and fragility.

name: GitGot
notes: Human-in-the-loop secret search tool. Not automated inside SOCMINT; a future GitHub exposure module can cover this use case through safer API-first collectors.

name: gitGraber
notes: Not integrated: GPL license, notification/cron behavior, token-heavy configuration and GitHub abuse-detection risks make it unsuitable for the default platform architecture.

name: Dark Web OSINT Tools
notes: Curated list only; no executable code or third-party visual interface is run or vendored because the repository does not publish a license file.

name: OnionSearch
notes: Candidate for a dedicated TOR lookup sidecar only through the existing TOR container, strict timeout, no login, no market interaction and no uncontrolled crawling.

name: Holehe
notes: Email account-existence checks are privacy-sensitive. Keep disabled unless the run is an explicitly authorized person/employee investigation with minimization and audit logging.

name: Toutatis
notes: Instagram-oriented user lookup is not enabled by default because it can require platform-sensitive handling. Use only for authorized public profile verification without credential/session reuse.

name: Mr.Holmes
notes: Broad person OSINT suite. Not bundled into the default runtime because overlapping modules increase false positives and data-minimization risk.

name: yesitsme
notes: Conditional person-correlation candidate only. Not installed by default because the repository license and account-checking behavior need deployment approval.

name: Awesome OSINT Arsenal
notes: Reference catalog only. Entries are not executed automatically; analysts can use it to expand allowlisted sources after review.

name: HowToFind OSINT Tools
notes: Reference catalog only. Useful for source discovery, not an executable collector in the platform.

name: Web Scraping Reference Set
notes: Reference implementations only. CyberDecisionEngine uses its own bounded public-search collectors with cache/backoff instead of importing arbitrary scraping code.

name: OpenClaw
notes: Kept as an optional gateway/assistant for analysis planning. It must not bypass authentication, captchas, rate limits or third-party controls; execution requires explicit approval and audited prompts.
